mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through lower cost of capital for corporate investments.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0% (1-month average) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening that raises borrowing costs and compresses corporate profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: doc:Monetary Policy Tightening and Equity Volatility
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% (1-month average).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent acceleration in housing starts (HOUST) and real consumption (RSAFS) signals robust aggregate demand that boosts corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise > 0.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST and RSAFS both rise > 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market (UNRATE < 4.0%), a monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates rising wage pressures that support consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% AND PAYEMS rises > 0.5% in the prior month
evidence_refs: doc:Labor Market Tightness and Equity Returns
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS rises > 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A lower unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates strong labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through immediate spending effects.
evidence_refs: doc:Unemployment Rate and Equity Market Correlation
failure_condition: The proportion of 5-day return periods with UNRATE below its 12-month average that yield negative returns exceeds 55% in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100 (INDPRO) signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and profit visibility, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signal aggressive monetary policy response to persistent inflation, raising real interest rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2% in the prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation environment (CPIAUCSL > 5.0% y/y), a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive tightening that increases real borrowing costs, driving negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 5.0% (y/y) AND FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1% in the prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 5.0% (y/y) and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1% in the prior month.
